hacker_news.title: If you're doing Monte Carlo try Knuth LGC
hacker_news.author: logicallee
hacker_news.content_context:
I was doing a monte carlo simulation involving a few million iterations and that didn't really need anything all that random. I remembered reading about a fast algorithm for very fast values (just a couple of ops), so I asked about this and was surprised that there is one. I just inserted it into my c code and it became ten times faster. If you're doing some monte carlo simulations where you don't need anything very random, give it a try.

before: 3.5 seconds. after: 0.42 seconds.

code I used:

 #include  static uint32_t seed = 1; // any non-zero value is fine static inline uint32_t fast_rand(void) { seed = seed * 1664525u + 1013904223u; // mod 2^32 is free return seed; } // then (example): int ch = fast_rand() % 1297 // where 1297 is the range.
(there's a slight bias when using % this way.) code gave the same results so it was still correct. you would adjust 1297 to the range you need an integer result in, this is from my example.

top_trends.title: If you're doing Monte Carlo try Knuth LGC
top_trends.author: logicallee
top_trends.content_context:
I was doing a monte carlo simulation involving a few million iterations and that didn't really need anything all that random. I remembered reading about a fast algorithm for very fast values (just a couple of ops), so I asked about this and was surprised that there is one. I just inserted it into my c code and it became ten times faster. If you're doing some monte carlo simulations where you don't need anything very random, give it a try.

before: 3.5 seconds. after: 0.42 seconds.

code I used:

 #include  static uint32_t seed = 1; // any non-zero value is fine static inline uint32_t fast_rand(void) { seed = seed * 1664525u + 1013904223u; // mod 2^32 is free return seed; } // then (example): int ch = fast_rand() % 1297 // where 1297 is the range.
(there's a slight bias when using % this way.) code gave the same results so it was still correct. you would adjust 1297 to the range you need an integer result in, this is from my example.

source_briefs.item_name: Llm.asm – Pure x86-64 Assembly for LLM Inference and Training
source_briefs.content_summary: 该项目包含三个完全用x86-64 NASM汇编语言编写的LLM项目，实现了Qwen3-0.6B模型的推理、一个可启动的裸机操作系统以及一个带有实时盲文TUI的Mini-GPT训练器。所有数学内核、引擎、分词器、线程池等均为手写汇编，总计17,252行代码，无任何C、C++、Rust或运行时依赖。
source_briefs.ai_comment: 这是一个极致的底层性能优化和教学示范项目，展示了在汇编层面实现现代AI计算核心的可能性，对理解LLM底层运作和极限优化有参考意义。

source_briefs.item_name: If you're doing Monte Carlo try Knuth LGC
source_briefs.content_summary: 作者在进行涉及数百万次迭代的蒙特卡洛模拟时，采用了Knuth的线性同余生成器（LGC）快速随机数算法。该算法仅需少量操作，使得代码运行速度提升了十倍（从3.5秒降至0.42秒）。文中提供了示例代码，并指出使用取模运算时存在轻微偏差。
source_briefs.ai_comment: 这是一个实用的性能优化技巧，提醒开发者在不需要高质量随机性的计算密集型场景中，可以考虑使用更轻量、更快的伪随机数生成器。
